items.title: GTA 6 didn't get as many Game Awards nominations as Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, but it was never going to
items.summary: Being a debut indie gives Sandfall the advantage
items.content:
Action Games Grand Theft Auto GTA 6 GTA 6 didn't get as many Game Awards nominations as Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, but it was never going to News By Scott McCrae Published 18 November 2026 Being a debut indie gives Sandfall the advantage

(Image credit: Rockstar) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter GTA 6 is leading the field at The Game Awards 2026, but it had no chance of breaking the record set by Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.

Not only was GTA 6 nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards before it even released, but it's the game with the most nominations at this year's show with eight. Following it is Resident Evil Requiem and Control Resonant, which both grabbed six nominations.

This matches Rockstar's previous effort, Red Dead Redemption 2, which also got eight nominations, but Death Stranding (10), The Last of Us Part 2 (11), Deathloop (9), God of War Ragnarök (11), and Baldur's Gate 3 (9) all received more nominations across the show's history. But even those juggernauts couldn't beat Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, which broke the record with 13 nominations last year.

So at the time of writing, Rockstar Games ' latest has eight award nominations. I say at the time of writing because it'll undoubtedly make an appearance in the Player's Voice category – which made for one of Clair Obscur's awards. Outside of that, Clair Obscur had three nominations in Best Performance for Jennifer English, Ben Starr , and Charlie Cox, so in theory, GTA could've had multiple nominees in that place. And of course, Clair Obscur had the best RPG award, while GTA is up for best Action/Adventure game.

However, Rockstar Games isn't an independent developer, being a part of Take-Two Interactive, and even if it was, it's not the debut title for the studio, locking it out of Best Debut Indie Game, too. So ultimately, no matter how good GTA 6 was, Rockstar would've needed four extra nominations on top of a Player's Voice nomination to even match Clair Obscur. Outside of a few more Best Performance nominations or Innovation in Accessibility, it probably wasn't possible.

GTA 6 could beat Clair Obscur's record-breaking Game Awards haul - but I wouldn't bet on it GTA 6 won't beat the GOTY record set by Baldur's Gate 3 and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 We got GTA 6 nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards before GTA 6 Of course, it had won Most Anticipated Game in the two years before, and the inevitable GTA Online will undoubtedly pick up some nominations in the future, so maybe one day it'll be close.

Passionate about the gaming world and its evolving culture, Steven has always wanted to combine his enjoyment of writing and love for gaming in a way that can provide insightful coverage for players and enthusiasts alike. Sign in to your TheGamer account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Although GTA 6 is set to sweep at The Game Awards this year, even Rockstar's long-awaited RPG doesn't have as many nominations as Sandfall Interactive's record-breaking Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 had last year. While the unique take on the turn-based RPG genre certainly helped, Expedition 33's staggering sales figures are also closely tied to its emotionally gripping narrative.

Even though Sandfall Interactive is still hard at work on a mysterious new game to follow up the release of Expedition 33, a recent announcement confirms that one of the key creators involved in its story has left the studio and won't be coming back for any future entries.

As reported by Eurogamer , Sandfall Interactive's narrative lead Jennifer Svedberg-Yen announced shortly after accepting a BAFTA for her work on Expedition 33 that she was no longer working with the development studio.

“When the dust settles, we will start thinking about DLC, but it's probably not going to be for a while.”

According to Jennifer herself, she had actually left the studio all the way back "in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition." Despite not giving a reason as to parting ways with the studio, Jennifer did have some ambitious goals for what she wants to work on next.

On top of Jennifer's plans to write "my own projects, my own stories," she also shared her goal of creating a fund to support up-and-coming narrative designers for video games, aiming to "bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers."

Sandfall Interactive Although Sandfall Interactive hasn't exactly been shy about the fact that Expedition 33's sequel isn't going to be an exact copy of the style of the original, the narrative lead's departure only emphasizes how much different the next game in the series will likely be.

Combined with the core principle of the studio being "its own personal taste" that Jeniffer notes won't "bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same," it sounds like Sandfall Interactive's Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 continuation or entirely new titles will still have plenty of surprises in store for open-minded fans while still keeping what made the original so spectacular.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer has ‘parted ways’ with Sandfall
items.summary: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has left Sandfall Interactive after her award-winning work on Clair Obscur…
items.content:
Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has left Sandfall Interactive after her award-winning work on Clair Obscur

Video Game News 18th Nov 2026 / 4:54 pm Posted by Rhiannon Bevan Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s lead narrative designer has left Sandfall Interactive.

After winning a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her work on the game, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen confirmed that she left Sandfall in July of this year.

As reported by GamesBeat , Svedberg-Yen did not go into detail about her departure: “I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition. We’ve parted ways.”

She added that she wants to work on her “own projects”, while helping to mentor up-and-coming writers.

“The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help,” Svedberg-Yen said. “That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.”

She also advocated for better working conditions for the creatives who make games. “I don’t believe in starving artists,” she said. “We should pay our people properly so everyone can have health care, have vacations.”

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 [76 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/clair-obscur-expedition-33/ >Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was a hit with players and critics alike when it launched in 2025. It went on to be an awards show darling, scooping up Game of the Year awards, including the much-sought-after GOTY at The Game Awards [526 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/events/the-game-awards/ >The Game Awards that year. In fact, it was the most nominated game in The Game Awards history , an accolade that hasn’t even been taken by Grand Theft Auto 6 [235 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/grand-theft-auto-6/ >Grand Theft Auto 6 , which leads in nominations this year .

Svedberg-Yen’s work was widely acclaimed, as many praised the game’s writing. Despite this, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was her first writing credit on a game. It remains to be seen if she works with another studio now that she has left Sandfall.

As for Sandfall, the studio is yet to reveal its next project following on from Clair Obscur’s success. It remains the studio’s only game release.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s Narrative Lead Reveals She Left Sandfall Interactive in July
items.summary: Following her win of the BAFTA Breakthrough US award, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen said that she wrapped up "some final stuff for Expedition."
items.content:
Following her win of the BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her work on 2025’s Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , the lead narrative designer on the RPG, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, has revealed that she is no longer working at studio Sandfall Interactive. Speaking to GamesBeat , she confirmed that she left the studio all the way back in July, and alluded to a bit of content that might be making its way to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

“No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition ,” she said when asked if she was still working at Sandfall Interactive. “We’ve parted ways.” When asked about why she decided to leave, she offered little in the way of details aside from noting that she wanted to work on “my own projects, my own stories”. This work also involves working to establish a fund that could mentor new and upcoming narrative designers in the games industry.

She spoke about this fund and how her background in finance helps her play a role in establishing it. As for why she was doing it, she said that in its current state, the games industry has trouble figuring out how to integrate narrative elements into the pipeline for a typical game’s development. Along with mentoring those new to the industry, the fund would also be an “incubation program” to help development teams make these integrations.

“One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers. This is the chicken-and-egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers, you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money, you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.”

“I’ve discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it’s a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.”

She also spoke about how times have been quite tough for the games industry, and that ultimately, “The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help.”

“That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.”

As for Svedberg-Yen’s last bit of work with Sandfall, the studio hasn’t really announced any major new content for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 yet. However, studio CEO Guillaume Broche has said that the team is going to “go a bit crazy” with its next major project .

items.title: 'A Lot of Studios Think of Narrative as a Skin' — Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's Lead Writer Has Left Sandfall to Help Devs Tell Better Stories
items.summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s lead writer has left Sandfall to help other game developers think about story from the outset.
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 ’s lead writer has left Sandfall to help other game developers think about story from the outset. Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the narrative lead for Expedition 33, won a BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. award earlier this year, and she’s since been consulting on stories across the industry.

Expedition 33 was her first video game (she came from a career in private equity), but it won more than 400 awards and received almost universal critical acclaim, in part due to its blend of real-time and traditional turn-based RPG mechanics, and partly because of its mysterious story, strong emotional beats, and brilliant characters.

Svedberg-Yen is now setting up a fund with the aim of advancing narrative design in video games and nurturing new writing talent.

“I feel that we are losing so much institutional knowledge,” Svedberg-Yen told GamesBeat . “We’re making it extraordinarily difficult for a younger generation of developers to have formative experiences. There’s so much disruption in the industry right now.”

Outside of the constant layoffs and upheaval in the industry, there’s also a sense, still, that narrative isn’t as respected as other parts of game design.

“A lot of studios think of narrative as a skin,” Svedberg-Yen said. “They think you can bring someone in later to make everything make sense.

“But when you start from the beginning, everyone is building from the same story and the different disciplines naturally reinforce each other.”

The award-winning writer believes this approach limits what games can achieve. Expedition 33 was designed with a narrative-first approach, with the game systems built around the story to reinforce the themes and pace the big moments out.

“Narrative was king,” she said. “It was always a narrative-first game. I think that’s why we were able to achieve the results that we did in terms of integrating all the different pieces into a wonderful collaborative whole. There was that consistency from the very beginning.”

According to Svedberg-Yen, she’s received messages from players about how Expedition 33 helped them deal with grief and navigate the world after suffering a personal loss.

Unfortunately, it doesn’t seem like we’ll see more of Svedberg-Yen’s work in video games any time soon. Outside of the fund, she has a couple of ideas for TV, but she left Sandfall in July “after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition.”

Following success at pretty much every major video game award show (most recently including scooping up Best Game at the BAFTA Awards ), Sandfall Interactive is now busy planning its next project. Details of that currently remain under wraps, though the suggestion is that it will be another adventure set in the same Clair Obscur universe .

"Wearing its inspirations on its sleeve, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 paints itself into the pantheon of great RPGs with a brilliant combat system and a gripping, harrowing story," IGN wrote in our Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 review , dubbing it a "modern RPG classic."

items.title: Expedition 33 Narrative Lead Officially Exits Award-Winning Studio
items.summary: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has left Sandfall Interactive
items.content:
Listen Thread Link copied to clipboard By Austin Manchester Published Nov 18, 2026, 10:32 AM EST Austin Manchester is a writer and editor living in New York City. At Polygon, he covers gaming and entertainment news, reviews new video games, interviews behind-the-scenes talent, and more. He enjoys discovering hidden gems and sharing them with Polygon's audience. Previously, he was the gaming editor for AIPT Comics and has written for other outlets like XDA, How-To Geek, and The List. He enjoys soulslikes, character-driven RPGs, and third-person shooters plucked straight out of the Xbox 360 era. He also likes to flex his non-video game nerdy knowledge sometimes, whether that's explaining who's who in the new Wolverine game or recommending a comic book series about a sentient sword. News ‘We’ve parted ways,’ Jennifer Svedberg-Yen said

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 seemingly came out of nowhere to capture the zeitgeist last year. Players enjoyed its old-school turn-based combat and marveled at its painterly environments, but the strong emotional writing captivated players the most. Sandfall Interactive CEO and creative director Guillaume Broche has previously said Clair Obscur is the franchise name and that Sandfall wants to tell more stories set in its world. However, those stories will be told without one of the Expedition 33 team's key members.

Lead writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen left Sandfall earlier this year. In a new interview with GamesBeat , she said, "I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition . We’ve parted ways."

Svedberg-Yen wants to focus on her own creative projects, like writing stories for TV and movies. She also wants to build "a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators." She wants video game stories to be elevated from being an afterthought and turned into a key element of the game that gets conceptualized from the outset alongside gameplay systems and everything else.

"I’ve done a lot of consulting work with different studios," Svedberg-Yen said. "I’ve discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it’s a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations." In her view, plenty of studios try to slap a story onto a game in the later stages of development, when it really should be integrated from the very beginning.

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive via Polygon Svedberg-Yen worked on Expedition 33 from the very beginning, and the game was always a narrative-first project. Its story and characters really resonated with players, and that was not lost on Svedberg-Yen. Players "felt that [the characters] were very three-dimensional, authentic characters. I’m very proud of our team for being able to achieve that."

Svedberg-Yen has lived a varied life, and she told Polygon a brief NASA simulation she took part in influenced the game's lineup of characters. "I got to experience being part of a small [crew]. And so I did base some of my thinking around what kind of people you would send on an expedition where it's not necessarily all military," she said.

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive She also shared how the beloved "wheee whooo" scene between Esquie and Verso was born out of her exhaustion. "That was me at three in the morning trying to come up with something," she told Polygon .

Video game development is a collaborative process, and the teams behind them are not monoliths; Svedberg-Yen wasn't the only contributing writer to Expedition 33 , and the team will carry on in her stead for its next project. However, some fans are already a bit worried about what her departure means for Sandfall.

As games take longer and longer to make, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 fans might have to wait a while to see what Sandfall is cooking up next. However, they can rest easy knowing happiness manager Monoco is still at the studio.

items.title: Clair Obscur Studio Has Lost One of Its Most Important Developers
items.content:
Jennifer Svedberg-Yen was the narrative lead on Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . She basically shaped the game's twisting and turning story, which many would argue is its greatest asset.

And so it's a bit of a gut punch to hear that she actually left developer Sandfall Interactive earlier this year — meaning that, unless she's already helped establish some of the project's narrative groundwork, she won't be involved with the studio's next game.

Svedberg-Yen dropped this bombshell in an interview with Gamesbeat , having just won a 'Breakthrough US' award at the BAFTAs for her work on Clair Obscur.

"I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition. We’ve parted ways," she explains.

It should be stressed that Svedberg-Yen really did spearhead the Game of the Year-winning title's story and tone right from the start; it wouldn't have been the experience that it was without her.

"I was the third person on the team. The team didn’t exist, actually. When I joined it was two guys who were still working at Ubisoft," she explains.

"The studio didn’t exist. It was the two co-founders and then me. Then we brought in the composer, and then the art director. Several months later we brought in the third co-founder, and then several months after that started the studio. So I was one of the founding members of the team."

Svedberg-Yen continues: "We came up with the idea together from the very start. It was always, from the very beginning, a narrative-focused game. It’s a narrative-first game. That’s what the creative director always said as well. Narrative is king."

And that approach is clear to see in the finished product, which has been lauded for its plot and characters ever since its release back in April of last year.

Svedberg-Yen goes on to talk about how important it is to establish narrative cohesion right off the bat, so that the whole development cycle is built around one vision. She thinks that too many games see story as something that can be slotted in over time, or simply added later on — and the whole thing suffers for it.

As for her own creative process, Svedberg-Yen provides some interesting insight: "I don’t think I could have written something like Expedition in my 20s, or even my 30s."

"I very much believe that one of the most powerful things we can do to train our ability to tell a good story is actually to live a rich life, to observe others, to learn how people work. If you’re trying to write about people, you must understand people."

Svedberg-Yen intends to work on her own projects going forward, which includes writing for film and TV — but she's also passionate about promoting the importance of narrative in video games.

As such, she wants to set up some kind of initiative, helping narrative-focused creatives make the next step in getting their games funded, and in turn, reshape the wider industry's perspective when it comes to storytelling. Sounds like a pretty noble goal to me.

items.title: Clair Obscur's narrative lead has left developer Sandfall Interactive after "wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition"
items.summary: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award, and left the developer back in July.
items.content:
Image credit: BAFTA/Eurogamer News by Dom Peppiatt Deputy Editorial Director Published on Nov. 18, 2026, 12:18 p.m. 19 comments Follow Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Prioritise us on Google Last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year . In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty big bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.

"No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a new generation of video game narrative designers.

"One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors."

Her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations."

"The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry."

Sandfall Interactive previously said its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste" , and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV shows and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.

We know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise , and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.

items.content:
Jennifer Svedberg-Yen , the narrative lead for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , won a BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. award, and she’s using the win to draw attention to a new fund for narrative leads in games.

This comes after she scored a big win on Clair Obscur — her first game as a narrative designer and writer after a career in private equity — a game with a strong narrative that won more than 400 awards. And she is now using her financial expertise to set up a fund dedicated to advance the art of narrative design.

The goal is to create new funding models that could nurture talent, rather than extract from it. And too often people forget that strong stories in games from The Last of Us to Resident Evil are what makes the best games so memorable.

Svedberg-Yen is still adjusting to life after Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. She discovered she won the award while sitting in a bagel shop and puzzling over a mysterious calendar invite.

But while the recognition celebrates her work on Sandfall Interactive’s breakout hit, Svedberg-Yen is already looking toward a larger mission: helping reshape how the game industry develops stories and supports creative talent. She left Sandfall back in July to focus on her new mission.

Svedberg-Yen wants to make sure that narrative is considered at the outset when a game is created. She feels that it’s too often treated as an afterthought in game development.

After consulting with numerous studios, she said she repeatedly encountered teams that viewed story as either scriptwriting or a layer added after core gameplay is complete. In her experience, that approach limits what a game can become.

“A lot of studios think of narrative as a skin,” Svedberg-Yen said. “They think you can bring someone in later to make everything make sense. But when you start from the beginning, everyone is building from the same story and the different disciplines naturally reinforce each other.”

That philosophy was embedded into Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 from the start in April 2020. Svedberg-Yen joined what would eventually become Sandfall Interactive before the studio formally existed. At the time, the team consisted of only two Ubisoft developers and herself.

Together they helped shape the game’s core concept and themes, making narrative a foundational pillar rather than an accessory.

“Narrative was king,” she said. “It was always a narrative-first game.”

Going forward, Svedberg-Yen wants to finish more of her own creative works, including stories intended for film and television, while continuing to explore ways to support fellow creators.

One of her techniques for writing is to have a rich life outside of work. If you get to know and observe people and hear their stories, you can walk in their shoes and have empathy for them.

“If you’re trying to write about people, you must understand people,” she said. “To understand people you need experience and empathy.”

items.title: GTA 6 Will Never Be Able to Beat Clair Obscur at The Game Awards
items.summary: It's almost impossible for GTA 6 to get more nominations, and more wins will be very difficult
items.content:
By Oli Welsh Published Nov 17, 2026, 7:51 AM EST Oli Welsh has been covering the business and culture of video games for two decades. He started out writing for Edge and other publications (specializing in MMOs and Blizzard, as cover for his World of Warcraft playtime) before joining Eurogamer, where he worked for 14 years as reviews editor, deputy editor, and editor-in-chief; Eurogamer won many Games Media Awards during his tenure. At Polygon, he writes about film and TV as well as games, and provides news, analysis, and criticism on the entertainment we love and the industries that make it, all from his home in London. He loves role-playing, racing, puzzles, tactics, exploration, storytelling, Nintendo, mysteries, spies, fantasy, reality, cars, and classic cinema. He wanted to be a movie critic when he grew up, and now he’s definitely grown up, and occasionally is one. He considers this a win. GOTY Watch It's almost impossible for GTA 6 to get more nominations, and more wins will be very difficult

GTA6 Rockstar Games Official Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Grand Theft Auto 6 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 6 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The triumph of Grand Theft Auto 6 at this year's Game Awards has seemed inevitable all year — especially in the face of what has turned out to be relatively weak competition . So you might assume that it's going to break records as it sweeps the board, just as it's going to break records commercially. But you'd be wrong.

The records for most nominations and most wins were set last year by Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Sandfall Interactive's RPG was nominated for 13 awards and won nine. It is practically, if not theoretically, impossible for GTA 6 to beat these totals.

Although the two games are very different, Clair Obscur was similarly dominant in the awards narrative. Like GTA 6 , nothing emerged all year that could realistically compete with it. And although it's a much smaller production, it excelled in the craft categories: performance, narrative, art direction, and music. It was nominated for, and won, most of the categories it was eligible for. The same looks likely to be true for GTA 6 . So how come it can't beat it?

Crucially, Clair Obscur was eligible for two categories where GTA 6 can't compete: Best Independent Game and Best Debut Indie Game. Some have quibbled with Clair Obscur 's definition as an indie, as it was a reasonably large-scale and well-funded production. But it was made by an independent studio for an indie-specialist publisher, so it's not an unreasonable definition. Either way, it happened.

Clair Obscur was nominated for Game of the Year, for all five craft categories (Game Direction, Narrative, Art Direction, Score and Music, Audio Design), and for the two indie categories. It had no less than three nominations in the Best Performance category (half the field). It was nominated for Best Role-Playing Game, its genre category. (Games can only be nominated in one genre category.) And it was nominated for the fan-voted Players' Voice award.

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive Let's assume that GTA 6 matches Clair Obscur beat-for-beat across GOTY, the craft categories, its genre category (Best Action/Adventure Game, in this case), and in Players' Voice. That seems a pretty safe assumption. Even if it can match Clair Obscur 's three performance nominations (a tall order, since jury members haven't spent as long with the characters), it would have to make up those two indie categories somewhere else to equal Clair Obscur 's record.

After ruling out the other genres, there are only a few other categories still on the table where that would be possible. GTA 6 is ineligible for most of them: Best Multiplayer, Ongoing Game, Mobile Game, VR/AR Game, and Community Support (as an unreleased game, it currently has no actual community). It hardly seems likely to get picked for Best Family Game or Games for Impact (however worthy it may or may not be). That only leaves Innovation in Accessibility. I have no idea about GTA 6 's credentials in this field. It might be great, although, given its late release, it will be untested by the public.

Lucia Caminos GTA6 Rockstar Games So, in order to match Clair Obscur 's record (never mind beat it), GTA 6 would have to be nominated for the accessibility award and get an unprecedented four Performance nominations. It's theoretically possible, but incredibly unlikely. I see GTA 6 netting out at 9 or 10 nominations, depending on whether both of the actors playing Jason and Lucia get nominated (or perhaps one of them plus a character part, such as Stephen Root's Brian Heder).

It will also be very difficult for GTA 6 to beat Clair Obscur 's nine wins. Clair Obscur ran an almost perfect game, winning in every category it was nominated for but two: Audio Design and Players' Voice. GTA 6 would have to win every single category I see it being nominated in to match that. It would need to be nominated in, and win, Innovation in Accessibility to beat it.

Neither scenario is impossible, but both are highly unlikely. These are two records GTA 6 is not going to break. In fact, given the unique circumstances surrounding Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 — an indie game with AAA production values and a beloved cast of actors — I expect these records are going to stand for a long, long time.

The timing of Rockstar's entry into the 2026 GOTY race could scarcely be more awkward

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team
